behavior: Aerial insectivore that twists and glides low over water and open ground, using relatively slow, deliberate wingbeats. Often forages alone or in small groups and perches on exposed branches, wires, and posts.
field_marks: Plain brown upperparts without bold markings
Dingy gray-brown throat and chest fading gradually to whitish belly
Small rounded head with a short, dark bill and dark eye
Short, nearly square tail with a shallow notch
habitat: Open areas, fields, waterways, and open woodland, especially near streams, ponds, and lakes. Nests singly or in small groups in earthen-bank burrows and in crevices or cavities in structures.
